title: An Open Recipe for IMO Gold: Training Nemotron for Olympiad Mathematics
data_curation: SFT corpus (released as Nemotron-Math-Proofs-v3-SFT): 15,879 hard AoPS proof problems from Nemotron-Math-Proofs-v1, selected by prior pass rates. DeepSeek-V4-Pro (Max mode) generates proofs up to 400K tokens, with up to three verifier-feedback refinement rounds (350K tokens), plus verifier traces (scores 0/0.5/1) and meta-verifier traces. Malformed, empty or length-capped outputs are filtered; proofs must have non-empty Solution and Self Evaluation sections; score-0 verifier traces are subsampled. Result: 414,890 examples over 15,818 problems (58,543 proof, 67,971 refinement, 236,360 verification, 52,016 meta-verification). RL set (Nemotron-Math-Proofs-v3-RL): 9,597 problems that Nemotron-3-Ultra solves in 1-3 of 4 attempts, judged by DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale. Evaluation: the new Nemotron-IMO-Bench (200 novel problems written with Titu Andreescu) and a 30-problem dev set (20 bench + 10 recent competition problems).
curriculum: Two independent specialists are branched from the Nemotron-3-Ultra 550B-A55B general-availability checkpoint rather than chained. One is long-context SFT (426K max sequence, ~1.6K optimizer steps at global batch 64, peak lr 1.5e-5 with warmup over 1,024 samples and cosine decay to 2e-6; step 1300 selected on 133 proof problems). The other is proof-generation RL started directly from GA. At test time a staged inference curriculum follows: round-1 ensemble generation, up to eight generate-verify-refine rounds, then a separate high-compute final-selection stage.
method: RL follows the DeepSeekMath-V2 reward design with the self-analysis reward removed (alpha=1, beta=0). It runs on asynchronous NeMo-RL in a PipelineRL-like setup with dynamic sampling, truncated importance sampling, and masking of low-probability tokens in positive samples when entropy exceeds 0.4. Settings: 128 prompts x 16 trajectories, AdamW (beta1=beta2=0.9) at lr 3e-6, max trajectory age 4 steps, 131K max sequence, 128 trainer + 128 inference + 16 judge GB200 nodes. Inference: GA, RL and SFT each sample 16 attempts under 8 strategy prompts (384 round-1 proofs). An RL+SFT panel gives 16 reference-free 0/0.5/1 judgments and accepts a proof only on unanimity. Otherwise the top 16 pool proofs are refined with critiques (192 attempts per round, at most 8 rounds). Finalists get 48 IMO-style 0-7 judgments (16 per checkpoint), ranked by mean with ties going to the shorter proof.
eval_metrics: Official IMO 2026 grading (0-7 per problem, 42 total). Development set: 30 problems scored by an independent GPT-5.5 / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Claude Opus 4.8 jury using the MathArena min-score reconciliation, reporting cumulative accepted-only and end-to-end scores. Dev-set end-to-end scores out of 210: GA 162, RL 180, SFT 165, ensemble 188. Verifier audit on 300 proofs: the RL+SFT 16/16 panel has a 1.1% false-accept and 81.3% false-reject rate, versus 31.6%/22.8% for GA alone. RL training is tracked on 133 proof problems graded by GPT-5.5. Compute accounting covers tokens and GB200 GPU-hours.
key_results: The fully natural-language system (no formal prover, tools or internet) scored 30/42 at IMO 2026, above the gold cutoff of 29: full marks on P1, P2, P4 and P5 and 1 point each on P3 and P6. All six submitted proofs were found within ~707M tokens and 1,464 GPU-hours (2.31B tokens and ~4,800 GPU-hours for the full run). Splitting round-1 budget across checkpoints beats doubling one: RL128+SFT64 scores 159 vs 139 for RL256.
evolution_note: The system follows the IMO 2025 natural-language gold results (Gemini Deep Think, OpenAI) and the generate-verify-refine line of Huang & Yang and DeepSeekMath-V2, whose generator/verifier/meta-verifier data design and reward it adopts. Its main contribution is openness: checkpoints, SFT/RL data, NeMo-RL/NeMo-Skills code, submitted proofs, compute accounting and a new uncontaminated benchmark. It also documents a shared blind spot of model-based verifiers, which credited P3/P6 proofs that officials gave 1 point, and finds that more elaborate refinement and triage schemes did not improve final coverage.
